editorial:
Ever wonder how fast a good life can fall apart? You get to see that happen here with Steve Keiver, a young lawyer who thinks he can play both sides. He starts taking quick cash from some sketchy gangsters to help them cheat the system, and he's actually too good at it. The mobsters love him, but the police are not fooled. You will feel the tension build as Inspector Matt Duggan starts closing in on Steve. It feels like a classic game of cat and mouse where one wrong move means you are finished.

What really works here is how the stakes keep getting higher. The acting is solid, and the story moves quickly without getting bogged down. While it might feel a bit dated to some, the drama is still very real. If you enjoy old-school crime stories, you should definitely check this out. You can find it by renting it on Apple TV or adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection if you like having the best picture quality on your shelf. It is a great pick for a rainy weekend afternoon.
endingExplained: Everything comes to a head when Steve realizes the mob will never let him leave. To save himself from prison or a coffin, he decides to turn state's evidence. He works with Inspector Duggan to set up a trap for the gangsters. In the final showdown, the police move in and arrest the mob bosses. Steve pays for his mistakes, but he manages to clear his name and avoid a life behind bars.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old crime dramas and stories about lawyers in trouble.
